reading.body:
This record is a single OpenStreetMap node in Italy tagged as a data center, with no confirmed operator, capacity, or status.

The entry carries a name, iZOOM.it, and coordinates in northern Italy near Parma, but no megawatts, no operator, no website, and no business registration. Its own research note states that confirmation failed because search quota ran out, not because the facility was investigated and found wanting. The ".it" in the name is consistent with an Italian hosting or domain business, which is a naming convention, not evidence of a data center.

For AI specifically, this tells nothing about compute capacity. A data center tag on a map is a claim about a building's use, not a measurement of power drawn, servers installed, or workload served. The absence of a megawatt figure is the honest part of the record: most facilities that matter to AI scaling have published or permitted power figures, and this one does not.

What the data does not cover is nearly everything. It cannot say whether iZOOM.it operates a rack in an office or a campus, whether it is active, or whether the tag is accurate. It should be read as an unverified map annotation awaiting a source, not as a facility in any inventory of Italian compute.
